conventions: The chapter describes the wicked distributively in the singular (הוּא, 3ms suffixes on יִתֶּן־לוֹ, בְּלִילוֹ, אֵינֶנּוּ, קַל הוּא) while the ASV writes the class in the plural ('they', 'them', 'their'). Align the pronoun the ASV wrote to the morpheme that denotes it (rule 18) and do not mark the number mismatch: 24.5 s016 → 'them', 24.6 s005 → 'their', 24.18 s002 → 'they', 24.23 s003 → 'them', 24.24 s005 → 'they'.

The ASV opens 24.2 and 24.9 with an existential-relative frame 'There are that' around a bare finite verb with an unwritten indefinite subject. No morpheme licenses the dummy, the copula or the relative, so the three words are one added unit doing one office (rule 2), headed on 'are'; the finite verb keeps only its lexical verb. Both verses are aligned that way.
report: Checked all 28 candidate lemmas against the verse dumps; every divergence is licensed by the ASV's own wording or by a distinct construction, and no unit is changed.

וְ: 24.22 'that' is rule 17's waw-plus-finite-verb relative, 24.15 'also' is rule 51, 24.12/24.24 'Yet'/'Yea' are rule 14 connectives read off the ASV; the remaining waws take the 'and' written for them.

הַ: every assimilated article takes a written 'the' where one stands before its noun (24.5, 24.6, 24.14, 24.16, 24.18) and is unrepresented where the ASV writes 'a' or nothing (24.14 'a thief', 24.20 'a tree', 24.22 'of life', 24.24 'as all others', 24.5 'for food'); 24.5 s019 → 'their' is rule 41's possessive written in the article's place. Consistent.

מִבְּלִי: 24.7 'without' and 24.8 'for want of' are both fused on the preposition and headed on בְּלִי (rules 30/48); the differing MACULA tags (Ncmsc vs Tn) do not change the analysis, and 24.10's bare בְּלִי → 'without' agrees.

לֹא: 'not' on the verb throughout; 'no'/'No' only where the ASV recasts the negation onto a nominal (24.15, 24.22), as rule 15 directs. 24.25's elliptical 'it be not so' on the sole anchor is defensible and its alternative is named in the note.

Added units read end to end: the two 'There are that' frames (24.2, 24.9) are treated identically; supplied lexical verbs ('yieldeth' 24.5, 'pass away' 24.18), supplied subjects ('God' 24.22, 24.23), supplied possessives with no suffix ('their' 24.11, 'his' 24.15), and supplied connectives/relatives ('So that' 24.10, 'So' 24.19, 'that' 24.21) are all added on the same terms. 24.12's 'populous' is the one folded supply, and it is a genuine double realization of מְתִים under rule 25 rather than a split with any other verse.

BSB disagreements: the four לְ tokens are the לֵאמֹר לְ (rule 27), a reflexive dative (24.16, rule 40) and two datives recast as bare indirect objects (24.5, 24.23, rule 40); the 24.24 paragogic nun is rule 32. All documented convention differences; none is an error.
No rule taught here generalises beyond what the contract already states; no promotions or amendments.
